summary: Re-audited independently on node1 (2026-11-01). `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean` on the file exits 0 with no output (no error, no 'declaration uses sorry', no warning); the only textual 'sorry' is the docstring's 'No `sorry`.' (l.15). No admit / native_decide / axiom / opaque / extern / set_option in the file. `lake build --no-build GXScaffold.Topology.PortlyExamples`: all targets up-to-date. `#print axioms` (via --stdin, nothing written) is exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for isPreconnected_compl_of_isTotallyDisconnected, isSkeletal_skeletonSpace_codim_two, isSkeletal_skeletonSpace, isSkeletal_of_isTotallyDisconnected, bowtie_counterexample, not_isLocallyStronglyConnected_bowtie, isSkeletal_of_tameKnot, isSkeletal_of_finite_surface, eq_empty_of_isSkeletal_real. `git diff HEAD` on the file deletes only the two sorry blocks and docstring prose: the statements of both target theorems and the definitions IsPureOfDim, skeletonSpace, IsLocallyStronglyConnected (and IsSkeletal/IsPortly in GX.Topology.Portly, untouched) are unchanged, so nothing was weakened to make the proofs go through. Item 4's Euclidean core uses a sound route without dimension theory (Janiszewski for disjoint closed sets through the exp-lifting on a simply connected, normal, locally path-connected space; Zorn on minimal closed separating sets; clopen separation of K from loc_compact_t2_tot_disc_iff_tot_sep; points do not separate by mathlib's isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank) — every hypothesis is discharged, none carries the conclusion. Item 3's codim-two proof builds its own local theory (openSimplex, carrier lemma via AffineIndependent.eq_of_sum_eq_sum_subtype, neighbourhoods B(x,r) ∩ G, pieces between a convex set and its closure chained by LSC). Fidelity vs RamcovGX.tex:367-374: the row is honestly `partial` and unmarked (item 3 false as written — bow-tie counterexample genuine, per DEC-27; item 2 under the disclosed locally-flat reading of 'tame', which for knots in 3-manifolds is the standard equivalent notion). LSC is satisfiable (one simplex), not vacuous (the bow-tie fails it, proved), and necessary for k = n-2 (it is exactly connectedness of a small open star minus the (n-2)-skeleton). Item 4's IsClosed hypothesis is automatic for a Cantor set in a Hausdorff manifold, and dim >= 2 is justified by eq_empty_of_isSkeletal_real ('wildly' presupposes n >= 3). The file has a single label and REPORT covers it; no declaration of the file clashes with a declaration in GX/ or in the other scaffold files (Basic.lean, Branched/Paths.lean), checked by grep over all 58 theorem/def names. Only minor issues remain.
